draft.title: Australian overseas aid
card: Overseas aid is money, goods, skills and services that one country gives to another to improve wellbeing. The Australian Government pays for Australia's aid from the federal budget, which comes mostly from taxes.
Most of Australia's aid goes to countries in the Indo-Pacific region, which includes Southeast Asia and the Pacific islands. These are close neighbours, and many have lower incomes.

Aid is spent on health, education, disaster recovery and economic growth. Examples are vaccination programs, school teacher training, rebuilding after a cyclone, and roads and ports that help trade and jobs.
Aid is one way to lift wellbeing in other countries. It is given by a government, so it is different from money raised by charities.
draft.remember: Australian aid is government support, mostly to Asia and the Pacific, for health, education, disaster recovery and economic growth.

a.q: Which situation shows Australian overseas aid?
opts: The Australian Government pays for a clinic in Vanuatu
A charity runs a sponsor-a-child appeal in Australia
A Queensland council builds a new local swimming pool
An Australian company opens a factory in Indonesia
a.why: Overseas aid is given by the Australian Government to another country to improve wellbeing, and a clinic in Vanuatu fits this. A charity appeal is tempting, but charities are not the government, so it is not Australian Government aid.
a.clue: Who gives the aid, and where does it go?

b.q: The federal budget pays for a new port in Tonga to help trade and jobs. Which area of aid is this, and who gives it?
opts: Economic growth, given by the Australian Government
Economic growth, given by Australian charities
Disaster recovery, given by the Australian Government
Education, given by Australian charities
b.why: A port that helps trade and jobs supports economic growth, and money from the federal budget means the Australian Government gives it. Disaster recovery is tempting, but no disaster is described. Charities raise their own money rather than spending the federal budget.
b.clue: What does the port help, and whose money pays for it?

a.best: The Australian Government pays for a clinic in Vanuatu

b.best: Economic growth, given by the Australian Government
